# Common brief: designing Panaudium factory presets

Panaudium is an open-source, sample-free synthesizer: every sound is generated by physical models,
formant/additive/granular synthesis or analog-style oscillators. The goal of the factory library is
Omnisphere-like DIVERSITY: a very wide range of clearly different sounds. Your presets will be rendered and
analysed automatically (loudness is normalised later; near-duplicates of existing presets will be removed),
so variety and plausibility matter more than polish.

## Read first (do not edit these)
- `src/dsp/Presets.h` — `PresetBuilder` API and the 35 existing presets in `addBank1` (study them as style
  examples and to AVOID duplicating them).
- `src/dsp/Params.h` — per-layer parameters (`LayerParam` enum, ranges and defaults in `buildParamDefs()`),
  `Engine` and `FilterType` enums, `engineLabels()` (what Timbre/Shape/Character/FM Depth do per engine),
  FX rack layout (`R_A`, `R_B`, `R_Common`; 3/3/4 slots).
- `src/dsp/Engines.h` — how each engine uses its controls (read the render functions to understand ranges).
- `src/dsp/fx/FxUnit.h` — `fxTable()`: every FX unit, its models and its knobs with real-world units/ranges.

## The builder API (all values are REAL units, not normalised)
```cpp
b.push_back(PB("Name", "Category")
    .oscA(E_Modal, timbre, shape, character)   // engine + its three macro controls (0..1)
    .A(L_Noise, 0.2f).A(L_FMDepth, 0.3f).A(L_FMRatio, 2)   // any LayerParam on layer A
    .uniA(voices, detuneCents, spread)          // unison
    .filtA(F_LP24, cutoffHz, reso)              // filter; also .A(L_KeyTrack,..).A(L_FiltEnv, octaves) ...
    .ampA(attack, decay, sustain, release)      // seconds / 0..1
    .A(L_FA, ..).A(L_FD, ..).A(L_FS, ..).A(L_FR, ..)          // filter envelope
    .A(L_L1Rate, hz).A(L_L1Pitch, semis).A(L_L1Cut, octaves)  // LFO1 (vibrato / filter wobble)
    .A(L_L2Rate, hz).A(L_L2Timbre, amt).A(L_L2Pan, amt)       // LFO2 (timbre morph / auto-pan)
    .oscB(...).B(...).uniB(...).filtB(...).ampB(...)          // layer B (calling any B setter turns B on)
    .fx(R_A, 0, FX_Stompbox, /*model*/2, /*mix*/1.f, { /*Drive*/0.7f, /*Tone*/0.4f, /*Level dB*/-6.f })
    .fx(R_Common, 0, FX_EQ, 0, 1.f, { 3.f, 120.f, -2.f, 900.f, 2.f, 9000.f })
    .chorus(mix, rateHz)        // = common slot 1
    .dly(mix, timeSec, feedback) // = common slot 2 (ping-pong)
    .rev(mix, size0to1, damp0to1) // = common slot 3 (Pro-Verb Hall); or call .fx(R_Common, 3, FX_ProVerb, model, mix, {...})
    .G(G_Glide, seconds)
    .done());
```
Knob lists in `.fx()` follow the knob order of that unit in `fxTable()`; you may give fewer values than
knobs (the rest stay at their defaults); use `NAN` to skip one (include <cmath> is already available).
Percent knobs take 0..1. Model is the index into the unit's model list. Note the init patch already has a
Pro-Verb (Hall, mix 0.25) in common slot 3; call `.noFx(R_Common, 3)` for a completely dry preset, or
`.rev(...)` / `.fx(R_Common, 3, ...)` to change it.

## Sound-design facts about the engines (important, learned from measurements)
- Plucked String, Modal: they are percussive; keep amp sustain high (0.9) and set decay with Character
  (Pluck: sustain/T60; Modal: decay) instead of the amp envelope; amp release still matters after note-off.
- Modal Timbre morphs mode sets: 0 = harmonic string/tube, 0.33 = marimba/bar, 0.67 = bell, 1.0 = membrane/
  plate (drums, gongs, bowls). Shape = mallet hardness. FM Depth adds inharmonic detuning. Noise > 0 excites
  the modes continuously (bowed/rubbed glass, singing bowls).
- Bowed String: Timbre = bow pressure, Shape = bow position (narrow, safe range), Character = sustain,
  FM Depth = wooden body resonance (0.3-0.8 sounds like a real instrument body). Plays best from C2 to E6.
- Blown Pipe (flute model): Timbre = breath noise, Shape = tone (dark..bright), Character = blowing
  pressure. Plays C2-A6. Breathy/airy instruments, pan flutes, ocarina-like (dark tone, little noise),
  recorder (bright), bottle blowing (high noise).
- Vocal: Timbre = vowel A-E-I-O-U (0..1), Shape = vocal tract size (0 = giant, 0.5 = adult, 1 = child),
  Character = breathiness. LFO2 > Timbre makes talking/morphing vowels.
- Analog/FM: Timbre morphs saw -> square -> triangle -> sine; Shape = pulse width/symmetry; Character above
  0.35 = hard sync sweep; FM Depth/Ratio = phase modulation by a sine (bells at ratio 3.5/7, e-piano at 1/14 etc.).
- Spectral (additive): Timbre = brightness, Shape = odd/even (1 = hollow/clarinet-like), Character =
  stretch/inharmonicity (bells/pianos), Drift = partial animation, FM Depth = partial spread (chorus).
- Granular: Timbre = grain density, Shape = grain size, Character = pitch scatter (high = octave/fifth
  sparkle), FM Depth = grain brightness.
- Atmos: noise through a tuned comb: Timbre = colour (dark..bright), Shape = pitch focus (0 = pure noise,
  0.9+ = clearly pitched whistle), Character = turbulence/gusts, FM Depth = colour resonance.
- Filters: F_Formant sweeps vowels with Cutoff (100 Hz..8 kHz); F_Comb tunes a comb to Cutoff (use
  KeyTrack 1 and Cutoff = 261.63 Hz to track the played note, or a multiple of it).
- Two layers + their own FX racks let you build hybrid sounds (e.g. bowed string + bell, pluck + pad,
  breath noise + vocal). Keep CPU sane: unison voices x heavy engines (Spectral, Granular, Modal) <= ~6.
- Levels: keep layer Levels 0.3-0.9; don't worry about overall loudness (it's normalised afterwards), but
  avoid huge resonances/feedback that would make one note much louder than others.

## Hard requirements
- Only edit your assigned bank file. Write presets inside its `addBankN(std::vector<Preset>& b)` function with
  `using PB = PresetBuilder;` at the top. Header-only C++17, compile-clean (check every enum/function name
  exists in the files above; e.g. FX enum names are FX_Stompbox, FX_Phaser, FX_Chorus, FX_Flanger,
  FX_Tremolo, FX_Rotary, FX_Delay, FX_ProVerb, FX_Innerspace, FX_Shimmer, FX_EQ, FX_Compressor, FX_LoFi,
  FX_RingShift, FX_Wah, FX_Tape, FX_Amp).
- Every preset name must be unique across the whole library (check bank 1 and avoid names likely used by the
  other bank: prefix nothing, just be specific and evocative, e.g. "Rusted Gamelan", not "Bell 2").
- Use the FX rack generously and idiomatically: per-layer racks (R_A/R_B) for character effects (drive,
  phaser, wah, amp, lo-fi, tape, ring mod) and the common rack for space (delay, Pro-Verb, Innerspace,
  Shimmer). At least half your presets should use a unit other than chorus/delay/reverb, and every FX unit
  type should appear at least twice across your bank.
- Above each preset write a one-line comment describing the intended sound.
- You cannot run shell commands (denied; a denied command aborts your run). Do not try.

## Report back
The number of presets, a table of name | category | engines | FX used, and anything you were unsure about.
